rationale: A 4h basis / premium mean-reversion strategy was tested because H-003 rejected daily price-band mean reversion but did not reject structural mean reversion in perpetual-market dislocations. Mark-index basis, premium index, and funding mechanics can create pressure for extreme dislocations to move back toward neutral. RETROSPECTIVE: this plan was authored after execution as part of WP-6c to extend the schema grammar to the remaining concluded candidates. The original H-010 pre-registration lives in research/hypotheses/H-010/HYPOTHESIS.md and was not schema-validated at the time.
hypothesis_to_test: A 4h basis / premium mean-reversion strategy on BTCUSDT perpetuals will generate OOS Sharpe >= 1.0 net of modeled costs, capture reversion in mark-index or premium extremes without relying on price-band oversold logic, keep turnover controlled enough that cost drag remains within D2-006 limits, and survive walk-forward validation with efficiency > 0.5.

additional_criteria: OOS Sharpe >= 1.0 net of modeled costs
Gate 2 passes under current evaluator semantics: dsr_val > 0.95 versus the expected maximum-SR benchmark from the registered trial count
Max drawdown <= 20% in any walk-forward fold
Parameter sensitivity: +/-25% parameter shift keeps Sharpe within 70% of baseline
No single 90-day window contributes > 60% of total PnL

Kill criteria from H-010 HYPOTHESIS.md apply: OOS Sharpe < 0.3, max drawdown > 35%, cost drag > 50% of gross PnL, basis extremes persisting rather than reverting, or results dominated by too few dislocation windows

data_requirements: 8h funding-rate stream for cashflow accounting: funding_8h
No separate IS/OOS split convention existed in repo truth for this baseline; DEC-0010 records full-period Sharpe in both trial-log Sharpe fields
author: WP-6c retrospective
